title_clean: To Vacchagotta on Fire — Aggivacchagotta Sutta (MN 72)
description_short: Bhante Bodhidhamma explores the Buddha's famous fire metaphor to explain what happens to an awakened being after death, revealing the futility of speculative views.
description_long:
In this profound teaching, Bhante Bodhidhamma examines the Aggivacchagotta Sutta (MN 72), where the Buddha addresses the wanderer Vacchagotta's persistent questions about the fate of awakened beings after death. When Vacchagotta becomes bewildered by the Buddha's refusal to affirm whether a Tathāgata exists, doesn't exist, both exists and doesn't exist, or neither exists nor doesn't exist after death, the Buddha employs his masterful fire metaphor. Just as an extinguished fire doesn't go anywhere but simply ceases its dependence on fuel, an awakened being transcends all categories of description. Bhante explains how this teaching cuts through speculative views (diṭṭhi) that create 'a thicket of views' leading only to suffering and confusion. The discourse illuminates the ineffable nature of awakening and the liberation that comes from releasing identification with the five khandhas. Through careful analysis of the ancient understanding of the four elements, Bhante reveals how this isn't annihilation but the cessation of grasping — pointing to the ultimate freedom of satipaññā (intuitive awareness) itself.
